hpi: Differential diagnosis by the pediatrician. Physiology of hyperbilirubinemia, Gilbert's syndrome, weight, breast milk jaundice, hemolytic disease of the newborn (ABO incompatibility), biliary atresia and G6PD deficiency. The key is to ensure that the baby is feeding well and that the mother is not overfeeding the baby. Although bilirubin levels can be obtained in the laboratory, it is essential for the pediatrician to determine if the infant is feeding well. This is important because if the infant continues to be breastfed the bilirubin levels may continue to rise. It is also important that breastfeeding is encouraged.

patient_voice.chief_complaint: I'm really worried about my baby's jaundice. It looks so yellow.
patient_voice.history: I noticed my baby was getting yellower each day. I’m scared it might be serious.
patient_voice.pain: I just want to make sure my baby is okay.
